t.1.215.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: He spoke to Arjuna and to Vāsudeva the Sātvata, the two foremost heroes of the world, who were standing near the Khāṇḍava forest.
t.1.215.3: Thus addressed, Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava then said to him: "With what food would you be satisfied? We two shall strive to obtain that food."
t.1.215.2: I am a brahmin who eats much; I always eat beyond measure. I beg of you two, Vārṣṇeya and Pārtha: may you grant me a single full satisfaction.
t.1.215.4: Thus addressed, the blessed one then spoke to those two heroes, who were at that moment saying, “What food shall be prepared?”
t.1.215.6: Indra always protects this Khāṇḍava forest; I am unable to burn it, guarded as it is by that great-souled one.
t.1.215.5: I do not truly wish to eat ordinary food; know me to be Pāvaka. Give me, you two, that food which is fitting for me.
t.1.215.7: Here there always dwells his friend, the serpent Takṣaka; for his sake the wielder of the thunderbolt, together with his host, guards this forest.
t.1.215.8: Many creatures there are protected along with it as a consequence; though I wish to burn it, I am unable to burn it because of the might of Śakra.
t.1.215.9: Seeing me blazing, he rains down upon me with the waters of the clouds; therefore, though I wish to burn it, I cannot burn the forest I desire.
t.1.215.10: Joined by you two as companions, both skilled in weapons, I would burn the Khāṇḍava forest; this is the food I have chosen.
t.1.215.12: When this had been said, Bībhatsu replied to Jātavedas, who was eager to burn the Khāṇḍava forest against the will of Śatakratu.
t.1.215.11: For you two, knowers of the supreme weapons, will thoroughly ward off those streams of water and the creatures on every side, everywhere.
t.1.215.13: I possess supreme weapons, divine and many, with which I could fight even many wielders of the thunderbolt.
t.1.215.14: O blessed one, I have no bow equal to the strength of my arms, one that could withstand my force as I exert myself in battle.
t.1.215.15: And I, shooting swiftly, have need of many inexhaustible arrows, for my chariot is not able to carry as many arrows as I desire.
t.1.215.16: And I would wish for divine white horses swift as the wind, and a chariot rumbling like the clouds, with a splendor like that of the sun.
t.1.215.18: Blessed one, you should tell me the means for accomplishing this task, by which I may hold back Indra as he rains upon the great forest.
t.1.215.17: Likewise, there is no weapon equal to the valor of Kṛṣṇa, with which Mādhava might slay Nāgas and Piśācas in battle.
t.1.215.19: Whatever is to be done by manly prowess, that we two shall accomplish, O Pāvaka; but you, blessed one, ought to give us capable instruments.
